items.title: The action functional of a force model with a potential presentation: the mechanical Lagrangian, its chart instance and its dimensions
items.statement:
Adopt one force model of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]]: $N\ge1$ particle labels
with fixed masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$ (clause (i)), an open nondegenerate time
window $I_{0}\subseteq\mathbb R$, an open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$
and a force map $F$ with the standing continuity and state-local-Lipschitz
hypotheses of clause (iii) of that postulate. Fix one inertial frame with adapted
coordinates $(t,x)$ and identify position tuples with points of
$\mathbb R^{3N}=(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$ ([[def-cm01-configuration]]); dimensions are
read by [[def-cm01-units]], inner products and norms are Euclidean
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), and differentiability classes are those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. Let $\mathsf M$ be the mass
operator of clause (d) of [[def-cm01-configuration]],
$\mathsf M(x_{1},\dots,x_{N})=(m_{1}x_{1},\dots,m_{N}x_{N})$, a symmetric
positive definite linear map of $\mathbb R^{3N}$.

**(a) Kinetic energy.** The **kinetic energy** of the labels at coordinate
velocity $v\in(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}=\mathbb R^{3N}$ is

$$K(v):=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^{N}m_{i}\,\lvert v_{i}\rvert_{2}^{2}=\frac12\,v\cdot\mathsf M v .$$

$K$ is the restriction of a $C^{\infty}$ function of $(\mathbb R^{3})^{N}$ and has
dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ (energy). Its Euclidean gradient is
$K'(v)=\mathsf M v$, because $\partial K/\partial v_{i}=m_{i}v_{i}$
([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]).

**(b) Mechanical Lagrangian of a potential presentation.** Let $(U,d)$ be a
potential presentation of the model's force map in the sense of clause (a) of
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]: a function
$U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{2}$ with dimension
$\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ and residual forces $d=(d_{1},\dots,d_{N})$ such that
$$F_{i}(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)+d_{i}(t,x,v)$$
on the state domain. The **mechanical Lagrangian of the presentation** is

$$L:I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad L(t,x,v):=K(v)-U(t,x).$$

$L$ is of class $C^{2}$ on its open domain and has dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$.
When $d\equiv0$ the presentation is a global potential model and $L$ is a
Lagrangian of the model itself; when $d\not\equiv0$, $L$ carries the potential
part only, and the residual force contribution $d$ is not included in $L$.
The
potential representative is part of the declared data: replacing $U$ by
$U+c(t)$ for differentiable $c:I_{0}\to\mathbb R$ replaces $L$ by $L-c(t)$
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] clause (c)).

**(c) Action, variations, stationarity.** Let $a<b$ be reals with
$[a,b]\subseteq I_{0}$. If $Q=\varnothing$, there is no map
$x:[a,b]\to Q$, so this clause has no action, variation or stationarity
instance. Assume $Q\ne\varnothing$ for the chart construction below, and put
$O:=I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$. The set $O$ is open and contains
$[a,b]\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$, so with $n:=3N$ the pair $(O,L)$ is a
time-dependent Lagrangian chart over $[a,b]\times Q$ in the sense of
[[def-cm-time-dependent-lagrangian-and-action]]. **Admissible
curves** (the $C^{2}$ curves $x:[a,b]\to Q$ with the extension convention of
that definition), **variations** $\eta$ with $\eta(a)=\eta(b)=0$, the
**action**

$$S(x):=\int_{a}^{b}L\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr)\,dt,$$

the **first variation** $\delta S(x)[\eta]$ and **stationarity** of $x$ are the
notions of [[def-cm-time-dependent-lagrangian-and-action]] instantiated at this
chart; the derivative $x'$ is the coordinate velocity ([[def-cm01-velocity-acceleration]]).
The action has dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$ (energy multiplied by time).
Write $E_{L}(x):[a,b]\to\mathbb R^{3N}$ for the Euler-Lagrange expression of
the instantiated chart.

**(d) Status.** This item defines the action functional and the Lagrangian of a
presentation from data already adopted in the model: no new force law, no
equation of motion and no measured value are introduced. The first variation
of $S$ exists for every admissible curve and variation and its formula, the
equivalence of stationarity with the vanishing of $E_{L}(x)$, and the relation
of both to the model's equation of motion are theorems of this page, not part
of the definition.
items.strategy: Define the kinetic energy, the mechanical Lagrangian of a declared potential presentation, the instantiated action, first variation and stationarity, and the dimensions; assert nothing beyond the definitions.
items.physical_scope: For a nonempty configuration domain, the action functional of the framework's force branch with a declared potential presentation: the kinetic energy of the labels in an inertial frame, the mechanical Lagrangian K - U of the presentation, the open chart and the action integral over C^2 curves with fixed endpoints, the first variation and stationarity, and the dimensions of these objects. If the force postulate is instantiated on an empty configuration domain, there are no curves and this item has no action or stationarity instances. It defines model-derived objects only: it asserts no equation of motion, no conservation law, no minimisation property and no empirical value, and it does not claim that any apparatus is described by a Lagrangian or by the potential branch.

references.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 2.1 'The Principle of Least Action', printed pages 10-13 (PDF pages 16-19): the action as the time integral of the Lagrangian, its variation and the stationarity condition

D. Cline, Variational Principles in Classical Mechanics (2nd edition, University of Rochester River Campus Libraries, open textbook, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Sections 5.1-5.2 and 6.1-6.2: the action functional, its first variation and the standard mechanical Lagrangian T - U

K. K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part CM: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), Section 2.1, chapter pages 1-2: generalized coordinates and the Lagrangian as kinetic minus potential energy

items.title: The first variation of the mechanical action and the Euler-Lagrange expression in model terms
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and the mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with masses
$m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$, time
window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and a potential
$U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{2}$
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]], [[def-cm01-configuration]]).
Let $a<b$ with $[a,b]\subseteq I_{0}$, let $x:[a,b]\to Q$ be a $C^{2}$
admissible curve and let $\eta$ be a variation of $x$
([[def-cm-time-dependent-lagrangian-and-action]]). Then:

1. $x+\varepsilon\eta$ is an admissible curve for every sufficiently small
   $|\varepsilon|$, the function $\varepsilon\mapsto S(x+\varepsilon\eta)$ is
   differentiable at $\varepsilon=0$, and

$$\delta S(x)[\eta]=\int_{a}^{b}\Bigl[-\nabla_{x}U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)\cdot\eta(t)+\mathsf M x'(t)\cdot\eta'(t)\Bigr]dt,$$

   where $\nabla_{x}U=(\nabla_{x_{1}}U,\dots,\nabla_{x_{N}}U)$ is the Euclidean
   gradient in the configuration slot and the dot is the Euclidean inner
   product of $\mathbb R^{3N}$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]);

2. the Euler-Lagrange expression of $L$ along $x$ is

$$E_{L}(x)(t)=-\Bigl(\mathsf M x''(t)+\nabla_{x}U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)\Bigr)\qquad(t\in[a,b]).$$

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch and on the declared
potential presentation; it selects no equation of motion and asserts no
empirical value.
items.strategy: Direct: instantiate the mathematical chart and first-variation suppliers at the mechanical Lagrangian and evaluate its configuration and velocity gradients.
items.physical_scope: The first variation of the action of a force model with a declared potential presentation, computed in the inertial chart: for every C^2 admissible curve and fixed-endpoint variation the variation exists and equals the integral of minus the potential gradient paired with the variation plus the mass-operator pairing of velocity with the variation's derivative, and the Euler-Lagrange expression of the mechanical Lagrangian is minus the sum of the mass-operator acceleration and the potential gradient. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted force branch, the declared potential presentation and the cited mathematical first-variation formula; it asserts no equation of motion, which is the subject of the following items.

references.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 2.1, printed pages 10-13 (PDF pages 16-19): the first variation of the action by integration by parts and the resulting Euler-Lagrange coefficient

D. Cline, Variational Principles in Classical Mechanics (2nd edition, University of Rochester River Campus Libraries, open textbook, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Section 5.2 (Euler's differential equation) and Section 5.8 (generalized coordinates in variational calculus)

I. Stewart, Advanced Classical Mechanics (MIT 8.09/8.309 Fall 2014 course text), Section 1.2 and Chapter 2: the equation of motion in Cartesian data and the Lagrangian formulation with the kinetic-minus-potential density

items.title: The stationary-action criterion and the potential-part Euler-Lagrange equation
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and the mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $C^{2}$ potential
$U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]).
Let $a<b$ with $[a,b]\subseteq I_{0}$, and let $x:[a,b]\to Q$ be a $C^{2}$
admissible curve ([[def-cm-time-dependent-lagrangian-and-action]]). Then the
following three conditions are equivalent:

1. $x$ is stationary for the action $S$ of $L$;
2. $E_{L}(x)(t)=0$ for every $t\in[a,b]$;
3. $\mathsf M x''(t)=-\nabla_{x}U\bigl(t,x(t)\bigr)$ for every $t\in[a,b]$.

Condition 3 is the model's equation of motion of the potential branch
([[post-cm02-force-superposition]] clause (iv)) written along the curve for the
presentation $(U,d)$ with the potential part alone: the residual forces $d$ do
not appear, and the statement is therefore a statement about the potential
part of the force map. No existence of curves satisfying these conditions is
asserted.
items.strategy: Direct: combine the mathematical stationarity characterisation with the model-terms Euler-Lagrange identity and read the result through the equation of motion.
items.physical_scope: The Euler-Lagrange equation of the mechanical Lagrangian of a declared potential presentation: for a C^2 curve of the model on a fixed interval, stationarity of the action, the vanishing of the Euler-Lagrange expression and the pointwise equation mass-operator acceleration equals minus the potential gradient are equivalent. The equivalence identifies the variational critical-point condition with the potential-part equation on the interval, and with the full model equation when d is identically zero; it is conditional on the adopted force branch and the declared presentation, and it asserts no solution existence, no minimisation and no empirical content.

references.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 2.1, printed pages 10-13 (PDF pages 16-19): stationarity of the action is equivalent to Lagrange's equations

D. Cline, Variational Principles in Classical Mechanics (2nd edition, University of Rochester River Campus Libraries, open textbook, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Sections 5.2-5.3 and 6.2: Euler's differential equation and the Newtonian plausibility argument for the standard Lagrangian

K. K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part CM: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), Section 2.1, chapter pages 1-2: Lagrange equations of motion for a system with kinetic minus potential energy

items.title: Stationary curves of the mechanical action are exactly the restrictions of the model's motions (global potential branch)
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $C^{2}$ potential
$U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]).
Assume the presentation has **no residual forces**, $d\equiv0$, so that the
force map itself is $F_{i}(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)$. Then:

1. **motions are stationary.** If $x:J\to Q$ is a motion of the model on an
   interval $J$ with nonempty interior ([[def-cm02-newtonian-flow]]) and
   $a<b$ with $[a,b]\subseteq J\cap I_{0}$, then the restriction $x|_{[a,b]}$
   is stationary for the action $S$ on $[a,b]$.

2. **stationary curves are restrictions of motions.** If $a<b$ with
   $[a,b]\subseteq I_{0}$ and $x:[a,b]\to Q$ is a $C^{2}$ admissible curve that
   is stationary for $S$, then $x$ is the restriction to $[a,b]$ of the
   maximal motion of the model through the initial datum
   $\bigl(a,x(a),x'(a)\bigr)$ (whose existence and uniqueness are
   [[pthm-cm02-ivp]] clause 4); in particular the maximal interval of that
   motion contains $[a,b]$.

3. **identification.** Consequently the $C^{2}$ curves $x:[a,b]\to Q$ that are
   stationary for the action are exactly the restrictions to $[a,b]$ of the
   motions of the model whose maximal interval contains $[a,b]$, and the model
   equation satisfied is $\mathsf M x''=-\nabla_{x}U$ on that interval.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch and on the declared
potential presentation with $d\equiv0$; it asserts no existence of stationary
curves for arbitrary endpoint data, no minimisation and no empirical value.
items.strategy: Direct: read stationarity as the model equation, then compare a stationary curve with the maximal motion through its datum using uniqueness and the compact continuation criterion.
items.physical_scope: The stationary-action principle for the global potential branch of the force model: every motion of the model restricts to a stationary curve of the mechanical action on each closed subinterval, and conversely every C^2 stationary curve on a closed interval is the restriction of the unique maximal motion of the model through its initial datum, so that the stationary curves are exactly the restrictions of motions. The equivalence is conditional on the adopted force branch, on the declared potential presentation with no residual forces, and on the cited existence, uniqueness and continuation theorems; it asserts no global existence, no minimisation property and no empirical statement.

references.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 2.1, printed pages 10-13 (PDF pages 16-19): Lagrange's equations as the stationarity condition of the action, equivalent to Newton's equations for a particle in a potential

D. Cline, Variational Principles in Classical Mechanics (2nd edition, University of Rochester River Campus Libraries, open textbook, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Section 6.2: the Newtonian plausibility argument identifying the stationary curves of the action T - U with the Newtonian trajectories

I. Stewart, Advanced Classical Mechanics (MIT 8.09/8.309 Fall 2014 course text), Section 1.2 and Chapter 2: uniqueness of Newtonian evolution from initial data and the equivalence of the Lagrangian and Newtonian descriptions

items.title: Time-dependent coordinate maps transform the potential-part equation into the substituted Euler-Lagrange equation
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $C^{2}$ potential
$U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]).
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3N}$ be open and nonempty and let
$X:\Omega\to Q$ be of class $C^{3}$ with $X_{q}(t,q)$ invertible for every
$(t,q)\in\Omega$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]],
[[def-invertible-euclidean-linear-map]]). Put

$$\widetilde O:=\bigl\{(t,q,v)\in\Omega\times\mathbb R^{3N}:\ \bigl(t,X(t,q),X_{t}(t,q)+X_{q}(t,q)v\bigr)\in I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}\bigr\},$$

$$\widetilde L(t,q,v):=L\bigl(t,X(t,q),\,X_{t}(t,q)+X_{q}(t,q)v\bigr).$$

Let $a<b$ and let $q:[a,b]\to\mathbb R^{3N}$ be a $C^{2}$ curve with
$(t,q(t),q'(t))\in\widetilde O$ for all $t\in[a,b]$; put $x(t):=X(t,q(t))$.
Then:

1. $\widetilde O$ is open, $\widetilde L$ is of class $C^{2}$ on it, and

$$E_{\widetilde L}(q)(t)=X_{q}\bigl(t,q(t)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}E_{L}(x)(t)\qquad(t\in[a,b]);$$

   consequently $E_{\widetilde L}(q)=0$ on $[a,b]$ if and only if
   $E_{L}(x)=0$ on $[a,b]$, and (by [[pthm-cm07-euler-lagrange-equations]])
   $q$ satisfies the substituted Euler-Lagrange equation if and only if the
   Cartesian description $x$ satisfies the model's potential-part equation
   $\mathsf M x''(t)=-\nabla_{x}U(t,x(t))$ on $[a,b]$.

2. If in addition there is an open set $W\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ with
   $q([a,b])\subseteq W$ and $[a,b]\times W\times\mathbb R^{3N}\subseteq\widetilde O$,
   then $(\widetilde O,\widetilde L)$ is a time-dependent Lagrangian chart over
   $[a,b]\times W$ and: $q$ is stationary for the substituted action
   $\widetilde S(q)=\int_{a}^{b}\widetilde L(t,q,q')\,dt$ if and only if $x$ is
   stationary for $S$.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, on the declared
potential presentation and on the smooth invertibility of $X$; the residual
forces $d$ do not enter, so clause 1 concerns the potential part of the force
map.
items.strategy: Direct: instantiate the mathematical covariance proposition at the mechanical Lagrangian and read the result through the model-terms identity and the chart dictionary.
items.physical_scope: Covariance of the model's equation of motion under a time-dependent coordinate map of the configuration domain: along a curve described by a C^3 map X with everywhere invertible configuration Jacobian, the Euler-Lagrange expression of the substituted Lagrangian is the transpose-Jacobian multiple of the inertial-chart expression, so the model's potential-part equation holds along the Cartesian description if and only if the substituted Euler-Lagrange equation holds along the coordinate description; when the chart condition holds, this is equivalent to stationarity of the substituted action. The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the potential presentation and the smooth invertibility of the coordinate map; it asserts nothing about constraints with fewer coordinates, which are treated separately, and no empirical claim.

references.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 2.2 'Changing Coordinate Systems', printed pages 13-16 (PDF pages 19-22): Lagrange's equations take the same form in any coordinate system, with the rotating-coordinate example

D. Cline, Variational Principles in Classical Mechanics (2nd edition, University of Rochester River Campus Libraries, open textbook, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Sections 6.3-6.4 and 5.8: Lagrange equations from d'Alembert's principle in generalized coordinates and generalized coordinates in variational calculus

K. K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part CM: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), Section 2.1, chapter pages 1-2: transformation of the Lagrangian description to arbitrary generalized coordinates

items.title: Total-derivative Lagrangians, the potential representative and scaling: invariant stationary curves with endpoint terms
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $C^{2}$ potential
$U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]).
Let $a<b$ with $[a,b]\subseteq I_{0}$, let
$F:I_0\times Q\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^{3}$ with dimension
$[F]=[S]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$, and define

$$L'(t,x,v):=L(t,x,v)+F_{t}(t,x)+F_{x}(t,x)\cdot v .$$

Then:

1. $L'$ is $C^{2}$ on $I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}$, has the same
   dimension as $L$, and for every $C^{2}$ admissible curve $x:[a,b]\to Q$ one
   has $E_{L'}(x)(t)=E_{L}(x)(t)$ for all $t\in[a,b]$ and

$$S'(x)=S(x)+F\bigl(b,x(b)\bigr)-F\bigl(a,x(a)\bigr),$$

   where $S'$ is the action of $L'$; consequently $x$ is stationary for $S'$
   if and only if $x$ is stationary for $S$, and, by
   [[pthm-cm07-euler-lagrange-equations]], both are equivalent to the model's
   potential-part equation $\mathsf M x''=-\nabla_{x}U$ along $x$.

2. **Potential representative.** Let $c:I_{0}\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^2$
   with dimension $[c]=[U]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ and antiderivative $C$
   (i.e. $C'=c$). Then $\widetilde U:=U+c$ remains of class $C^2$ and is the
   representative of [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] clause (c),
   with Lagrangian $\widetilde L=K-\widetilde U$. Then
   $\widetilde L=L+M$ where $M(t,x,v)=F_{t}+F_{x}\cdot v$ for
   $F(t,x):=-C(t)$, so clause 1 applies: the actions of $L$ and
   $\widetilde L$ differ by $C(a)-C(b)$, independently of the curve, and the
   stationary curves and the model's equation are unchanged.

3. **Scaling.** For every dimensionless real $\lambda\ne0$ one has
   $E_{\lambda L}(x)=\lambda E_{L}(x)$ pointwise, so the stationary curves of
   the Lagrangian $\lambda L$ coincide with those of $L$; the value $\lambda=0$
   is excluded because the zero Lagrangian has every curve stationary.

The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch and presentation; it
asserts no minimisation, no conservation law and no empirical content, and it
does not remove the need to declare which representative and normalisation are
used by an energy statement.
items.strategy: Direct: apply the mathematical gauge proposition to the mechanical chart and evaluate the potential-representative substitution and the scaling.
items.physical_scope: Gauge properties of the mechanical action of a declared potential presentation: adding to the Lagrangian the total time derivative of a C^3 function defined on the chart time-configuration domain, with the function carrying action units, changes the action by endpoint values only and leaves the Euler-Lagrange expression, the stationary curves and the model's stationary-action equation unchanged; changing the potential representative by a sufficiently regular function of time alone is an instance and shifts the action by a constant-free endpoint term; multiplying the Lagrangian by a nonzero dimensionless constant leaves the stationary curves unchanged. The statements are conditional on the adopted force branch and presentation and assert no minimisation and no empirical content.

references.title: D. Cline, Variational Principles in Classical Mechanics (2nd edition, University of Rochester River Campus Libraries, open textbook, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Section 9.3: equivalent Lagrangians under addition of a total time derivative, and the role of the arbitrary constant in the potential

D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (Cambridge lecture notes, January 2015 printing), Section 2.5.7, printed page 37 (PDF page 43): the equations of motion are invariant under addition of a total derivative to the Lagrangian

K. K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part CM: Classical Mechanics (title page last edited September 1, 2026), Section 1.3, chapter pages 7-8: the additive constant of the potential and the energy reference

items.title: Generalized-coordinate maps of the model, the substituted Lagrangian, the kinetic metric and generalized forces
items.statement:
Adopt the force model with potential presentation $(U,d)$ and mechanical
Lagrangian $L=K-U$ of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]], with
masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N}>0$, open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$,
time window $I_{0}$, mass operator $\mathsf M$ and $C^{2}$ potential
$U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]).
Dimensions are read by [[def-cm01-units]]; gradients and Jacobians are those of
[[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]], transposes those of
[[def-transpose-of-a-matrix]], and $C^{r}$ classes those of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]].

**(a) Generalized-coordinate map.** Let $r\ge1$ and let
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^{r}$ be open and nonempty. A **generalized-coordinate
map of the model** is a map $X:\Omega\to Q$ of class $C^{3}$ whose derivative
$DX(q)$ is injective for every $q\in\Omega$
([[def-euclidean-submersions-and-immersions]]: an immersion); the coordinates
$q=(q_{1},\dots,q_{r})$ each carry a declared dimension $\gamma_{i}$ and unit
fixed as part of the model declaration. When $r=3N$, injectivity makes
$DX(q):\mathbb R^{3N}\to\mathbb R^{3N}$ a bijection: its kernel is $\{0\}$,
so rank-nullity gives image dimension $3N$, equal to the target dimension.
The inverse is linear: if $y_{1}=DX(q)u_{1}$ and $y_{2}=DX(q)u_{2}$, then
linearity and uniqueness of preimages give
$DX(q)^{-1}(a y_{1}+b y_{2})=a u_{1}+b u_{2}$. Thus $DX(q)$ is invertible in
the sense of [[def-invertible-euclidean-linear-map]]. The inverse-function
theorem and its higher-regularity result
([[thm-euclidean-inverse-function-theorem]],
[[thm-higher-regularity-of-local-inverses]]) make $X$ a local $C^{3}$
diffeomorphism at each point. This local property does not imply that $X$ is
globally one-to-one: call $X$ a global coordinate chart onto $X(\Omega)$ only
when it is also injective. The other intended case is $r=3N-k$ for an integer
$k$ with $1\le k\le3N-1$, where $X$ may be a surjective immersion of a regular
holonomic-constraint locus as in clause (d); injectivity is not required there.
The **admissible coordinate curves** are the $C^{2}$ maps $q:J\to\Omega$ on an
interval $J\subseteq I_{0}$ with nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]); each such
curve induces the configuration curve $x:=X\circ q:J\to Q$.

**(b) Substituted Lagrangian and kinetic metric.** For a generalized-coordinate
map $X$ define

$$\widetilde L:I_{0}\times\Omega\times\mathbb R^{r}\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad \widetilde L(t,q,v):=L\bigl(t,X(q),DX(q)v\bigr)=\tfrac12\,v^{\mathsf T}G(q)v-\widetilde U(t,q),$$

with the **kinetic metric** and the substituted potential

$$G(q):=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX(q),\qquad \widetilde U(t,q):=U\bigl(t,X(q)\bigr).$$

$G(q)$ is symmetric and positive definite, because $DX(q)$ is injective and
$\mathsf M$ is symmetric positive definite
([[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]], [[def-linear-map]],
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]]); its entry
$G_{ij}$ has dimension $\mu\ell^{2}\gamma_{i}^{-1}\gamma_{j}^{-1}$ and the
quadratic quantity $\frac12v^{\mathsf T}G(q)v$ has dimension
$\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$ for every choice of coordinate dimensions.
$\widetilde L$ is of class $C^{2}$; the **substituted action** of an admissible
coordinate curve $q:[a,b]\to\Omega$ with $[a,b]\subseteq I_{0}$ is
$\widetilde S(q):=\int_{a}^{b}\widetilde L(t,q(t),q'(t))dt$ whenever the
chart conventions of [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] apply to
$\widetilde L$, and the **Lagrange operator** of $\widetilde L$ is

$$\Lambda(\widetilde L)(q)(t):=\frac{d}{dt}\Bigl(\frac{\partial\widetilde L}{\partial v}\bigl(t,q(t),q'(t)\bigr)\Bigr)-\frac{\partial\widetilde L}{\partial q}\bigl(t,q(t),q'(t)\bigr)\in\mathbb R^{r}.$$

**(c) Generalized forces.** Let $f:I_{0}\times Q\times\mathbb R^{3N}\to\mathbb R^{3N}$
be a force field of the model's standing regularity
([[post-cm02-force-superposition]] clause (iii)) — for instance the residual
force $d$ of the presentation, or the model's full force map $F$. Its
**generalized force** in the coordinates $X$ is

$$Q_{f}(t,q,v):=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}f\bigl(t,X(q),DX(q)v\bigr)\in\mathbb R^{r};$$

its $i$-th component has the dimension of energy per unit of the coordinate
$q_{i}$, namely $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}\gamma_{i}^{-1}$: the Jacobian factor
$\partial X_{a}/\partial q_{i}$ carries the dimension $\ell\gamma_{i}^{-1}$ and
the force $f_{a}$ the dimension $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$. Thus $Q_{f}\cdot\delta q$
has energy dimension; for a length-valued coordinate $Q_{f,i}$ has force
dimension, and for a dimensionless angle it has torque dimension
$\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$. For the presentation
$(U,d)$ write $Q^{\mathrm{res}}:=Q_{d}$ for the generalized force of the
residual part; when $d\equiv0$ one has $Q^{\mathrm{res}}\equiv0$.

**(d) Constraint parametrizations.** Let a regular holonomic-constraint datum
$(O,k,g_{c})$ of [[def-cm06-holonomic-constraint-model]] be given, where
$g_{c}:=G$ is the constraint map called $G$ in that definition; this separate
notation distinguishes it from the kinetic matrix $G(q)$ in clause (b). Let
$\mathcal C\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ be its time-independent configuration
locus, so $\Sigma=\{(t,x)\in O:x\in\mathcal C\}$ (the scleronomic case).
A **parametrization of the constrained configurations** is a
generalized-coordinate map $X:\Omega\to Q$ with $r=3N-k$,
$X(\Omega)=\mathcal C\cap Q$, and $(t,X(q))\in O$ for all
$(t,q)\in I_{0}\times\Omega$. Thus $X$ covers every constrained configuration,
but a configuration may have more than one coordinate representative; a
covering or other surjective immersion is allowed. Injectivity is an optional
additional condition for applications that require unique coordinates. Each
admissible coordinate curve induces a constrained curve family with permitted
velocity; the reduction theorem of this page also identifies the virtual
displacements with the image of $DX$.

**(e) Declared Lagrange equations.** With the data of clauses (a)-(c), the
model with presentation $(U,d)$ **declares as its Lagrange equations in the
coordinates $X$**

$$\Lambda(\widetilde L)(q)(t)=Q^{\mathrm{res}}\bigl(t,q(t),q'(t)\bigr)\qquad(t\in J),$$

posed for $C^{2}$ admissible coordinate curves $q:J\to\Omega$. These equations
are part of the coordinate description: for $d\equiv0$ they reduce to the
Euler-Lagrange equation $\Lambda(\widetilde L)(q)=0$ of the substituted
Lagrangian. For a chart ($r=3N$), the transport identity of
[[prop-cm-coordinate-covariance-of-the-euler-lagrange-expression]] clause 4,
applied to the time-independent map $X$, gives
$\Lambda(\widetilde L)=DX^{\mathsf T}(\mathsf Mx''-F+d)$ along
$x=X\circ q$: here $L_v=\mathsf Mx'$ and $L_x=-\nabla_xU$, while
$F=-\nabla_xU+d$. Hence $\Lambda(\widetilde L)=DX^{\mathsf T}d$
is equivalent to $\mathsf Mx''=F$, since $DX^{\mathsf T}$ is invertible.
On any interval $J$, the transport calculation applies on compact
subintervals around each interior time and extends to included endpoints
by continuity of these expressions. Whether
the same equations describe an ideal constrained motion for a
parametrization of clause (d) is a separate statement, proved as the reduction
theorem of this page; it is not part of this definition.

**(f) Status.** This item defines the dictionary between the Cartesian and the
generalized-coordinate descriptions: the coordinate map, the substituted
Lagrangian, the kinetic metric, generalized forces and the declared Lagrange
equations. It adopts no force law beyond the model's presentation, asserts no
solution existence and makes no empirical claim; the equivalence of the
declared equations with the model's Cartesian equation (for charts) and with
the ideal constrained equation (for parametrizations) is proved on this page.
items.strategy: Define the generalized-coordinate dictionary: immersion or chart, substituted Lagrangian, kinetic metric, generalized forces and the declared Lagrange equations; no equivalence is asserted here.
items.physical_scope: The dictionary from the model's Cartesian description to generalized coordinates: a C^3 configuration map that is an immersion; when the coordinate count is 3N, an everywhere-invertible Jacobian gives local coordinate charts, while a global chart onto the image additionally requires injectivity; for a regular holonomic-constraint locus the parametrization is a surjective immersion and may cover a configuration more than once. The item also defines the substituted Lagrangian and kinetic metric, generalized forces as Jacobian-transpose multiples, and the declared Lagrange equations with residual generalized forces. It defines objects and a model class only; it asserts no equivalence with the constrained equation of motion, which is the reduction theorem of this page, and no empirical claim.

items.title: Transport of the Euler-Lagrange expression under a C^3 map: E of the substituted Lagrangian is the Jacobian-transpose multiple of E of the ambient Lagrangian
items.statement:
Let $n,m\ge1$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^{n}$ and
$Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{m}$ be open and nonempty, and let
$X:\Omega\to Q$ be of class $C^{3}$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an
open interval and let $L:J\times Q\times\mathbb R^{m}\to\mathbb R$
be of class $C^{2}$, with gradients $L_{x}$ and $L_{w}$ in the second and third
slots ([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]],
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). Define

$$\widetilde L:J\times\Omega\times\mathbb R^{n}\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad \widetilde L(t,q,v):=L\bigl(t,X(q),DX(q)v\bigr).$$

Then $\widetilde L$ is of class $C^{2}$, and for every interval $J'\subseteq J$
with nonempty interior and every $C^{2}$ curve $q:J'\to\Omega$
([[def-interval]], [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]) with
$x:=X\circ q$ one has, writing $\widetilde L_{q}$ and $\widetilde L_{v}$ for the
gradients of $\widetilde L$ in the second and third slots,

$$\widetilde L_{q}\bigl(t,q(t),q'(t)\bigr)-\frac{d}{dt}\Bigl(\widetilde L_{v}\bigl(t,q(t),q'(t)\bigr)\Bigr)=DX\bigl(q(t)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}\Bigl(L_{x}\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr)-\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(L_{w}(t,x(t),x'(t))\bigr)\Bigr)$$

for every $t\in J'$. In words: the Euler-Lagrange expression of the
substituted Lagrangian is the transpose-Jacobian multiple of the
Euler-Lagrange expression of the ambient Lagrangian. No rank or invertibility
condition on $DX$ is assumed; the identity holds for every $C^{3}$ map $X$,
square or not.
items.strategy: Direct: differentiate the substituted Lagrangian in both slots by the chain rule and cancel the parametrization-correction terms.

items.title: Ideal scleronomic holonomic constraints: the substituted Lagrange equations are equivalent to the constrained model equation
items.statement:
Adopt the force-branch data of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]]: $N_{p}\ge1$
labelled particles with masses $m_{1},\dots,m_{N_{p}}>0$, an open time window
$I_{0}$, an open configuration domain $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N_{p}}$ and a force map
$F$ with the standing regularity; adopt a regular holonomic-constraint datum
$(O,k,g_{c})$ of [[def-cm06-holonomic-constraint-model]], where $g_{c}:=G$
is the constraint map named $G$ in that definition, and the ideal-reaction law
of [[post-cm06-ideal-reaction-law]]. Assume the datum is **scleronomic with
time-independent locus** $\mathcal C\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N_{p}}$:

$$\Sigma=\bigl\{(t,x)\in O:\ x\in\mathcal C\bigr\}.$$

Let $(U,d)$ be a potential presentation of $F$ in the sense of clause (a) of
[[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]], so that
$F_{i}(t,x,v)=-\nabla_{x_{i}}U(t,x)+d_{i}(t,x,v)$. Let $r:=3N_{p}-k$,
let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^{r}$ be open and nonempty, and let
$X:\Omega\to Q$ be a **parametrization of the constrained configurations** in
the sense of clause (d) of [[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]]:
$X$ is of class $C^{3}$, $DX(q)$ is injective for every $q\in\Omega$,
$X(\Omega)=\mathcal C\cap Q$ and $(t,X(q))\in O$ for all
$(t,q)\in I_{0}\times\Omega$. Injectivity of $X$ is not assumed: the image
condition requires coverage of the constrained configurations, while multiple
coordinate representatives are permitted. Define the kinetic matrix,
substituted potential, substituted Lagrangian and
residual generalized force

$$\mathsf G(q):=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX(q),\qquad \widetilde U(t,q):=U\bigl(t,X(q)\bigr),\qquad \widetilde L(t,q,v):=\tfrac12\,v^{\mathsf T}\mathsf G(q)v-\widetilde U(t,q),$$

$$Q^{\mathrm{res}}(t,q,v):=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}d\bigl(t,X(q),DX(q)v\bigr).$$

Let $J\subseteq I_{0}$ be an interval with nonempty interior, let $q:J\to\Omega$
be a $C^{2}$ curve and put $x:=X\circ q$. Then the following are equivalent:

1. $x$ is a constrained motion of the model with an ideal reaction field: there
   is a continuous $R:J\to\mathbb R^{3N_{p}}$ with
   $\mathsf M x''(t)=F\bigl(t,x(t),x'(t)\bigr)+R(t)$ and
   $R(t)\cdot\delta=0$ for every $t\in J$ and every virtual displacement
   $\delta\in\ker D_{x}g_{c}(t,x(t))$;
2. $\Lambda(\widetilde L)(q)(t)=Q^{\mathrm{res}}\bigl(t,q(t),q'(t)\bigr)$ for
   every $t\in J$, i.e. the declared Lagrange equations of
   [[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]] hold along $q$.

If these hold, then:

3. the reaction is unique: $R(t)=\mathsf M x''(t)-F(t,x(t),x'(t))$ for every
   $t\in J$, and there is a unique continuous
   $\lambda:J\to\mathbb R^{k}$ with
   $R(t)=D_{x}g_{c}(t,x(t))^{\mathsf T}\lambda(t)$;
   if the declared constraint components have dimensions $\gamma_{\alpha}$,
   then $[\lambda_{\alpha}]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}/\gamma_{\alpha}$;
4. the virtual displacements at $x(t)$ are exactly the image of $DX(q(t))$,
   $\ker D_{x}g_{c}(t,x(t))=DX(q(t))\bigl(\mathbb R^{r}\bigr)$;
5. the statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the presentation,
   the scleronomic regular constraint datum and the ideal-reaction law. No
   solution existence, no uniqueness of the coordinate curve for given data
   and no empirical content are asserted.
items.strategy: Direct: identify virtual displacements with the image of the parametrization, translate the ideal reaction into the transpose condition, and combine the transport identity with the model-terms Euler-Lagrange expression.
items.physical_scope: The elimination of ideal scleronomic holonomic constraints by parametrization: for a global C^3 surjective immersion onto the constrained configurations of a scleronomic regular holonomic datum, a C^2 coordinate curve describes an ideal constrained motion of the force model exactly when it solves the declared Lagrange equations of the substituted Lagrangian with the residual generalized force; multiple coordinate representatives of one configuration are allowed. The reaction is then uniquely determined, annihilates the virtual displacements and admits the unique continuous multiplier. The statement is conditional on the adopted force branch, the potential presentation, the constraint datum with its rank hypothesis and the ideal-reaction law; it asserts no solution existence, no uniqueness of the coordinate curve for given data and no empirical claim.

items.title: Scope of the stationary-action formulation: no minimisation, regular mechanical Lagrangians, no general velocity-constraint equivalence and empirical status
items.statement:
- **Stationarity is not minimisation.** The defining condition of
  [[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]] is the vanishing of the first
  variation for all fixed-endpoint variations, and
  [[pthm-cm07-euler-lagrange-equations]] identifies it with the model's
  equation. It is not claimed that a stationary curve minimises the action, and
  no second-variation or convexity hypothesis is imposed on this page:
  [[rem-cm-scope-of-stationarity]] records the explicit quadratic model in
  which stationary curves are not local minima, and the verification page of
  this pair checks the analogous phenomenon for an oscillator of the model
  class.

- **The mechanical branch is regular.** For the mechanical Lagrangians of this
  page the velocity Hessian in a chart is the kinetic matrix
  $G(q)=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}\mathsf M\,DX(q)$ (or $\mathsf M$ in Cartesian data),
  which is symmetric positive definite because $DX(q)$ is injective and
  $\mathsf M$ is; [[prop-cm-mechanical-chart-lagrangian-is-hyperregular]]
  proves that such a chart Lagrangian is hyperregular with the explicit
  Legendre inverse, so no failure of invertibility of the Legendre map
  [[def-cm-legendre-map-in-a-time-dependent-chart]] occurs on this branch and
  the Euler-Lagrange equations determine the coordinate accelerations. A
  singular velocity Hessian — for which the Legendre map is not locally
  invertible and the second-order equations need not determine accelerations —
  is outside the hypotheses of every theorem on this page; the admissible
  coordinate maps of the generalized-coordinate definition of this page
  exclude it by injectivity of $DX$ and positive definiteness of $\mathsf M$.

- **Velocity constraints are not covered by the action principle.** The
  reduction theorem of this page applies to ideal *holonomic* constraints. For
  a genuine velocity constraint the unrestricted minimisation of the action of
  the substituted Lagrangian, or of an augmented action with multipliers, is a
  different law from the d'Alembert equation of the preceding page:
  [[def-cm-nonholonomic-velocity-constraint-law]] defines both prescriptions
  for the constraint $z'=xy'$ and
  [[cex-cm-dalembert-and-vakonomic-evolutions-differ]] proves that their
  evolutions differ from the same initial data. Therefore the model's
  nonholonomic branch is not obtained by "imposing a constraint inside the
  action", and the examples page quantifies the discrepancy. Any identification
  of the two prescriptions requires its own justification and is not asserted
  here.

- **Empirical status.** The equivalence of the stationary-action condition with
  the model's equation of motion is a conditional theorem of the adopted force
  branch, the declared potential presentation and the cited mathematics: it
  does not establish that nature extremises or stationarises an action, and it
  adds no empirical content beyond the force model and its potential
  presentation. When the presentation has residual forces the equations acquire
  the generalized forces of the generalized-coordinate definition of this page
  and the pure action reading is lost; comparing predictions with observations
  tests the force law and the apparatus, not the variational reformulation.
  [[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]] clause (c) supplies the further
  reminder that the potential and the Lagrangian are defined only up to the
  declared normalization, so no numerical value of the action is a model
  prediction without fixing that convention.

- **Not asserted.** No global existence of stationary curves, no theory of
  minimisers in function spaces, no conjugate-point or Morse-theoretic
  statements, no free- or variable-endpoint problems, and no field-theoretic
  or infinite-dimensional actions are part of this page; the boundary-value
  non-uniqueness of the oscillator, for instance, is recorded in the
  verification page of the mathematics track, not here.
items.strategy: Scope audit: record the non-minimisation warning, the regularity of the mechanical branch, the nonholonomic exclusion and the empirical status, with the cited suppliers.
items.physical_scope: Scope audit of the stationary-action formulation of the force model: stationarity is not minimisation; the mechanical Lagrangians of this framework are regular and the chart Legendre map is hyperregular, so the second-order equations determine accelerations, while degenerate Lagrangians are excluded; unrestricted-action and d'Alembert dynamics are not generally equivalent for velocity constraints, as the cited counterexample shows for its specified model and data; and the stationary-action equivalence is a conditional theorem of the model, not empirical evidence. The remark asserts no new physical claim.

title: Stationary action and Lagrangian dynamics — Examples

items.title: The free particle: the unique stationary curve between fixed endpoints is the straight uniform motion, and it minimises the action
items.statement:
Declare a one-label model of the force branch of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N=1$, mass $m>0$, time window
$I_{0}=\mathbb R$, configuration domain $Q=\mathbb R^{3}$ and zero force map
$F\equiv0$; this is the global potential model with potential $U\equiv0$ and no
residual forces ([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]), whose
mechanical Lagrangian is
$$L(t,x,v)=\tfrac12\,m\lvert v\rvert_{2}^{2}$$
([[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]]). Let $a<b$, let
$x_{a},x_{b}\in\mathbb R^{3}$, and consider the $C^{2}$ curves
$x:[a,b]\to\mathbb R^{3}$ with $x(a)=x_{a}$ and $x(b)=x_{b}$. Under the
units of [[def-cm01-units]], $[m]=\mu$, $[x]=[x_{a}]=[x_{b}]=\ell$,
$[t]=[a]=[b]=\tau$, and $[x']=\ell\tau^{-1}$.

Then:

1. $x$ is stationary for the action $S$ if and only if $x$ is affine,
   $x(t)=x_{a}+v_{0}(t-a)$ with constant $v_{0}\in\mathbb R^{3}$; consequently
   there is exactly one stationary curve with the prescribed endpoints,
   $$x_{*}(t):=x_{a}+\frac{t-a}{b-a}\,(x_{b}-x_{a}),\qquad x_{*}'=\frac{x_{b}-x_{a}}{b-a}.$$
2. For every variation $\eta$ of $x_{*}$ one has the exact identity
   $$S(x_{*}+\eta)-S(x_{*})=\frac m2\int_{a}^{b}\lvert\eta'(t)\rvert_{2}^{2}\,dt\ge0,$$
   with equality if and only if $\eta=0$; hence $x_{*}$ is the unique minimiser
   of $S$ in the class of $C^{2}$ curves with these endpoints.
3. The global affine curve $x_{\max}:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^{3}$ defined by
   $x_{\max}(t)=x_{a}+v_{0}(t-a)$, with
   $v_{0}:=(x_{b}-x_{a})/(b-a)$, is the unique maximal motion through the datum
   $\bigl(a,x_{a},v_{0}\bigr)$, and $x_{*}=x_{\max}|_{[a,b]}$.

All quantities are model values; no measurement is reported.
items.strategy: Direct: solve the second-order free equation, then expand the action of a varied curve and integrate by parts.
items.physical_scope: A worked check of the stationary-action equivalence on the free one-label model: zero force map, zero potential, Cartesian Lagrangian of a free particle; on every closed time interval the stationary curves are exactly the affine uniform motions, for each pair of endpoint configurations there is exactly one, and the action difference to the stationary curve is a nonnegative quadratic functional of the variation, so the stationary curve is a minimiser within the fixed-endpoint class. The mass, position, time and velocity carry dimensions mass, length, time and length per time, respectively. All quantities are model values under the declared idealization of a particle subject to no force.

items.title: The harmonic oscillator on a long interval: the stationary curve is neither a local minimum nor a local maximum
items.statement:
Fix a duration $T>0$ and declare a one-label model of the force branch of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N=1$, mass $m>0$, time window
$I_{0}=\mathbb R$, configuration domain $Q=\mathbb R^{3}$, a fixed unit vector
$e\in\mathbb R^{3}$ with dimensionless components, and force map
$F(t,x,v)=-k(e\cdot x)e$ with constant $k>0$. This is the global potential
model with $U(x)=\tfrac12k(e\cdot x)^{2}$ and no residual forces
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]), with mechanical Lagrangian
$$L(t,x,v)=\tfrac12m\lvert v\rvert_{2}^{2}-\tfrac12k(e\cdot x)^{2}$$
([[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]]). Under
[[def-cm01-units]], $[m]=\mu$, $[e]=1$, $[x]=\ell$, $[t]=[T]=\tau$,
$[k]=\mu\tau^{-2}$, $[\omega]=\tau^{-1}$ and $[\ell_{0}]=\ell$, where
$\omega:=\sqrt{k/m}>0$. Fix a length scale $\ell_{0}>0$ and let
$\eta_{n}(t):=\ell_{0}\sin(n\pi t/T)e$; the scalar $\varepsilon$ below is
dimensionless. Consider curves on $[0,T]$.

Then:

1. the zero curve $x_{*}\equiv0$ is stationary for the action $S$;
2. for every integer $n\ge1$ the map $\eta_{n}$ is a variation of $x_{*}$,
   and for every dimensionless real $\varepsilon$ one has the exact
   identity
   $$S(\varepsilon\eta_{n})=\frac{mT\ell_{0}^{2}}{4}\,\varepsilon^{2}\Bigl(\Bigl(\frac{n\pi}{T}\Bigr)^{2}-\omega^{2}\Bigr);$$
3. if $T>\pi/\omega$, then $S(\varepsilon\eta_{1})<0$ and
   $S(\varepsilon\eta_{n})>0$ for every integer $n>\omega T/\pi$ and every
   $\varepsilon\ne0$; since $\varepsilon\eta_{n}\to0$ in the dimensionless
   $C^{2}$ metric defined below as $\varepsilon\to0$, the stationary curve
   $x_{*}$ is neither a local minimiser nor a local maximiser in that topology;
4. if $0<T<\pi/\omega$, then $S(\varepsilon\eta_{n})>0$ for every $n\ge1$ and
   every $\varepsilon\ne0$: every variation in this family increases the
   action, and no claim of global minimality is made.
items.strategy: Direct: evaluate the action of the scaled sine variations in closed form and read off the two signs.
items.physical_scope: A worked check that stationarity is not minimisation, on a harmonic oscillator embedded in three-dimensional configuration space and moving along one fixed unit vector, with positive stiffness: on intervals longer than pi divided by the angular frequency, arbitrarily small fixed-endpoint variations in the declared dimensionless C^2 metric around the zero stationary curve produce both strictly larger and strictly smaller actions, so the stationary curve is neither a local minimiser nor a local maximiser; on shorter intervals every sine-mode variation in the checked family increases the action. The computation uses exact model actions and exact trigonometric integrals; no experimental values are reported.

items.title: Cylindrical coordinates for one label: the kinetic metric m diag(1, r^2, 1) and the coordinate form of the model's equation
items.statement:
Declare a one-label model of the force branch of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N=1$, mass $m>0$, time window
$I_{0}=\mathbb R$, configuration domain $Q=\mathbb R^{3}$ and a global
potential presentation $F(t,x,v)=-\nabla U(t,x)$ with $C^{2}$ potential
$U:I_{0}\times Q\to\mathbb R$ and no residual forces
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]); the mechanical Lagrangian is
$L(t,x,v)=\tfrac12m\lvert v\rvert_{2}^{2}-U(t,x)$
([[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]]). Let
$\Omega:=\{(r,\theta,z)\in\mathbb R^{3}:r>0\}$ and define the cylindrical
coordinate map
$$X(r,\theta,z):=\bigl(r\cos\theta,\ r\sin\theta,\ z\bigr),\qquad X:\Omega\longrightarrow Q ,$$
with substituted Lagrangian and kinetic metric
$$\widetilde L(t,r,\theta,z,\dot r,\dot\theta,\dot z)=\tfrac12m\bigl(\dot r^{2}+r^{2}\dot\theta^{2}+\dot z^{2}\bigr)-\widetilde U(t,r,\theta,z),\qquad \widetilde U(t,r,\theta,z):=U(t,X(r,\theta,z)),$$
$$G(r,\theta,z)=DX(r,\theta,z)^{\mathsf T}\,(mI_{3})\,DX(r,\theta,z)=m\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\ 0&r^{2}&0\\ 0&0&1\end{pmatrix}.$$

Under [[def-cm01-units]], $[m]=\mu$, $[r]=[z]=\ell$, $[t]=\tau$ and
$[\theta]=1$ (dimensionless angle); $[\dot r]=[\dot z]=\ell\tau^{-1}$,
$[\dot\theta]=\tau^{-1}$, and $[U]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$. The configuration image is
$Q_{\mathrm{cyl}}:=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^{3}:x^{2}+y^{2}>0\}$, which omits
the $z$-axis.

Then:

1. $X$ is a $C^{\infty}$ map with everywhere invertible Jacobian, hence a local diffeomorphism at every point of $\Omega$, so the covariance theorem applies to it; its image is $Q_{\mathrm{cyl}}$, it is periodic in $\theta$, and it is not a global chart of $Q$. The coordinate equations are interpreted on these local charts or along a chosen coordinate lift.
2. the Euler-Lagrange equations of $\widetilde L$ are exactly
   $$m\bigl(\ddot r-r\dot\theta^{2}\bigr)=-\partial_{r}\widetilde U,\qquad m\bigl(r^{2}\ddot\theta+2r\dot r\dot\theta\bigr)=-\partial_{\theta}\widetilde U,\qquad m\ddot z=-\partial_{z}\widetilde U,$$
   which are the coordinate components of $m x''=-\nabla U(t,x)$ along
   $x=X(r,\theta,z)$;
3. consequently, for $a<b$ and a $C^{2}$ curve
   $(r,\theta,z):[a,b]\to\Omega$ with
   $x:=X\circ(r,\theta,z)$, the coordinate curve is stationary for the
   substituted action if and only if the Cartesian curve $x$ satisfies the
   model's equation of motion on $[a,b]$.
items.strategy: Direct: compute the Jacobian, the kinetic metric and the Euler-Lagrange equations of the substituted Lagrangian, and identify them with the Cartesian equation in the orthonormal cylindrical frame.
items.physical_scope: A worked check of the coordinate-covariance theorem on cylindrical coordinates for one labelled particle of mass m in a declared potential presentation: the map covers the open region off the z-axis periodically and supplies local coordinates there, but is not a global chart of all configuration space; the substituted Lagrangian has kinetic metric m diag(1, r^2, 1), the coordinate Euler-Lagrange equations are exactly the Cartesian equation written in the cylindrical frame, and the Cartesian stationary curves correspond to coordinate lifts. The radial and axial coordinates have length dimension, the angle is dimensionless, and no measurement is reported.

items.title: A total-derivative Lagrangian on explicit data: the endpoint term and the unchanged equations
items.statement:
Declare a one-label model of the force branch of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N=1$, mass $m>0$, time window
$I_{0}=\mathbb R$, configuration domain $Q=\mathbb R^{3}$ and zero force map; the
mechanical Lagrangian is $L(t,x,v)=\tfrac12m\lvert v\rvert_{2}^{2}$
([[def-cm07-action-and-mechanical-lagrangian]]). Let $t_{0}>0$ be a time scale,
fix the interval $[t_{0},2t_{0}]$, a dimensioned parameter $\alpha$ with
$[\alpha]=\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$, and the $C^{2}$ function

$$F(t,x):=\alpha\,t\,x_{1},\qquad L'(t,x,v):=L(t,x,v)+F_{t}(t,x)+F_{x}(t,x)\cdot v=\tfrac12m\lvert v\rvert_{2}^{2}+\alpha x_{1}+\alpha t\,v_{1},$$

so that $L'$ is the Lagrangian $L$ plus the total time derivative of $F$
([[pthm-cm07-boundary-terms-and-gauge]]). Under [[def-cm01-units]],
$[m]=\mu$, $[x]=\ell$, $[t]=[t_{0}]=\tau$, and $[F]=[S]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$.
Fix a unit vector $e_{1}=(1,0,0)$ and a velocity $v_{0}$ with
$[v_{0}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$, and consider the dimensionally consistent affine
curve $x_{*}(t):=v_{0}(t-t_{0})$ on $[t_{0},2t_{0}]$.

Then:

1. for every $C^{2}$ curve $x:[t_{0},2t_{0}]\to\mathbb R^{3}$ one has
   $E_{L'}(x)(t)=E_{L}(x)(t)=-m x''(t)$ at every $t\in[t_{0},2t_{0}]$, and the
   stationary curves of $S$ and $S'$ coincide;
2. for the curve $x_{*}$ the actions satisfy
   $$S'(x_{*})-S(x_{*})=F(2t_{0},x_{*}(2t_{0}))-F(t_{0},x_{*}(t_{0}))=2\alpha t_{0}^{2}(e_{1}\cdot v_{0}),$$
   with $S(x_{*})=\tfrac12m\lvert v_{0}\rvert_{2}^{2}t_{0}$ and
   $S'(x_{*})=S(x_{*})+2\alpha t_{0}^{2}(e_{1}\cdot v_{0})$;
3. for the reference-unit choice $m=1\,\mathrm{kg}$, $t_{0}=1\,\mathrm{s}$,
   $v_{0}=(1\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1})e_{1}$ and
   $\alpha=1\,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-2}$, these values are
   $S=0.5\,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm{m}^{2}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$,
   $S'=2.5\,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm{m}^{2}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ and endpoint term
   $2\,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm{m}^{2}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, all of dimension
   $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$, while the equation of motion and stationary curves
   are unchanged.
items.strategy: Direct: compute the two Euler-Lagrange expressions on a general curve and evaluate the endpoint term and both actions on explicit data.
items.physical_scope: A worked gauge check on the free one-label model in three-dimensional configuration space: adding the total time derivative of F(t,x)=alpha*t*x_1 to the free Lagrangian changes the action by endpoint values and leaves the Euler-Lagrange expression equal to the original one, hence leaves stationary curves and the model equation unchanged. The position is a vector of length dimension, time has time dimension, alpha has force dimension, and F has action dimension. The potential normalization U + gamma*t is the special case F = -gamma*t^2/2, with gamma of energy-per-time dimension. The values are exact model values of a declared computation.

items.title: The unrestricted action principle fails for the normalized nonholonomic relation $z_s = x y_s$: the d'Alembert motion is not vakonomic
items.statement:
Adopt the constraint model of [[def-cm-nonholonomic-velocity-constraint-law]]
in dimensionless normalized variables: let $s=t/T_{0}$ be dimensionless time
and $(x,y,z)=\mathbf r/L_{0}\in\mathbb R^{3}$ be dimensionless coordinates,
where $T_{0}>0$, $L_{0}>0$ and $m_{0}>0$ are reference quantities with
$[T_{0}]=\tau$, $[L_{0}]=\ell$ and $[m_{0}]=\mu$. Primes below mean differentiation with respect to $s$. The
normalized unit-mass equations have zero applied force and velocity constraint
$z_{s}=xy_{s}$; in physical variables this is
$\dot r_{z}=(r_{x}/L_{0})\dot r_{y}$, which is dimensionally consistent.
The physical kinetic action is $m_{0}L_{0}^{2}/T_{0}$ times the normalized
action; scaling the augmented multiplier by $m_{0}L_{0}/T_{0}$ makes its
augmented action the same positive multiple of the normalized one, preserving
stationarity. Physical reactions scale as $m_{0}L_{0}/T_{0}^{2}$ times
normalized reactions, and physical virtual displacements scale as $L_{0}$, so
the zero-virtual-work condition is preserved. In these normalized variables
the d'Alembert prescription is
$x_{ss}=0$, $y_{ss}=-\lambda x$, $z_{ss}=\lambda$ with
$\lambda=x_{s}y_{s}/(1+x^{2})$ along motions, and the vakonomic prescription
is $x_{ss}=-\eta y_{s}$, $y_{ss}=\eta_{s}x+\eta x_{s}$,
$z_{ss}=-\eta_{s}$ for the normalized multiplier $\eta$. Consider the
normalized initial data
$$(x,y,z)(0)=(0,0,0),\qquad(x_{s},y_{s},z_{s})(0)=(1,1,0).$$

Then:

1. the curve
   $$x(s):=s,\qquad y(s):=\int_{0}^{s}\frac{du}{\sqrt{1+u^{2}}},\qquad z(s):=\int_{0}^{s}u\,y_{s}(u)\,du=\sqrt{1+s^{2}}-1$$
   is a d'Alembert motion with these data on $\mathbb R$, and it satisfies
   $y_{s}(s)=(1+s^{2})^{-1/2}>0$ and
   $y_{ss}(s)=-s\,(1+s^{2})^{-3/2}$ for every $s\in\mathbb R$, so
   $y_{ss}(s)\ne0$ whenever $s\ne0$;
2. $y_{ss}(1/2)=-4/(5\sqrt{5})\ne0$;
3. consequently this d'Alembert motion is not a vakonomic motion of the same
   constraint with the same data: on any nondegenerate interval where a
   vakonomic pair for this curve is stationary, $x_{ss}=0$ and $y_{s}>0$
   force $\eta\equiv0$, and then the vakonomic equation forces
   $y_{ss}\equiv0$. Every nondegenerate interval contains some $s\ne0$, which
   contradicts clause 1;
4. hence, for this normalized model and initial data, the vakonomic
   stationary-action prescription does not reproduce the d'Alembert motion.
   This conclusion concerns the augmented-action prescription defined by the
   vakonomic law above; it makes no claim about a separately specified
   minimization problem or other variational prescriptions.
items.strategy: Direct: substitute the displayed curve into the d'Alembert equations, evaluate the curvature terms, and derive the contradiction with the vakonomic system.
items.physical_scope: A worked check in dimensionless normalized coordinates and time, with physical length and time scales declared, on the nonholonomic relation z_s = x y_s: the d'Alembert motion from the stated normalized initial data has strictly positive y_s and nonzero y_{ss} for s>0, so it cannot satisfy the vakonomic (unrestricted-action) equations of the same constraint, which force y_{ss} to vanish wherever x_{ss} does. Thus these two prescriptions differ for this model and data, so no general equivalence holds. The example reports exact model computations, not measurements.

items.title: The planar pendulum by constraint elimination: kinetic metric, Lagrange equation and the ideal reaction recovered
items.statement:
Declare a one-label model of the force branch of
[[post-cm02-force-superposition]] with $N=1$, mass $m>0$, time window
$I_{0}=\mathbb R$, configuration domain $Q=\mathbb R^{3}$ and force map
$$F(t,(x,y,z),v):=(0,-mg,0)$$
with constant $g>0$: the global potential model of potential
$U(x,y,z)=mgy$ and no residual forces
([[def-cm03-potential-and-mechanical-energy]]). Under [[def-cm01-units]],
$[m]=\mu$, $[x]=[y]=[z]=[l]=\ell$, $[t]=\tau$, $[g]=\ell\tau^{-2}$,
and $[U]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$; the angle
$\theta$ is dimensionless. Fix $l>0$ and constrain the
label to the circle of radius $l$ in the plane $z=0$ by the regular
holonomic-constraint datum of [[def-cm06-holonomic-constraint-model]]
$$O:=\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{3},\qquad k:=2,\qquad g_{c}(x,y,z):=\bigl(x^{2}+y^{2}-l^{2},\ z\bigr),$$
and adopt the ideal-reaction law of [[post-cm06-ideal-reaction-law]]. The
locus is the time-independent set
$\mathcal C=\{(x,y,z):x^{2}+y^{2}=l^{2},\ z=0\}$, so the datum is scleronomic, and the
map
$$X:\mathbb R\longrightarrow Q,\qquad X(\theta):=\bigl(l\sin\theta,\ -l\cos\theta,\ 0\bigr)$$
is a surjective immersion of the constrained configurations in the sense of
[[def-cm07-generalized-coordinates-and-forces]]. It is periodic and not
one-to-one; the definition and reduction theorem allow these multiple angle
representatives.

Then, with $r=3N-k=1$, kinetic metric $\mathsf G(\theta)=ml^{2}$, substituted
potential $\widetilde U(\theta)=-mgl\cos\theta$ and substituted Lagrangian
$$\widetilde L(\theta,\dot\theta)=\tfrac12ml^{2}\dot\theta^{2}+mgl\cos\theta,$$
the following hold:

1. for every interval $J\subseteq I_{0}=\mathbb R$ with nonempty interior and
   every $C^{2}$ curve $\theta:J\to\mathbb R$ with $x:=X\circ\theta$, the
   curve $\theta$ solves the Lagrange equation
   $\Lambda(\widetilde L)(\theta)=0$, i.e.
   $$ml^{2}\theta''+mgl\sin\theta=0,$$
   if and only if $x$ is a constrained motion with ideal reaction;
2. when this holds, the reaction is
   $$R(t)=D_{x}g_{c}(x(t))^{\mathsf T}\begin{pmatrix}\lambda_{1}(t)\\\lambda_{2}(t)\end{pmatrix}=-m\bigl(l\theta'(t)^{2}+g\cos\theta(t)\bigr)\bigl(\sin\theta(t),-\cos\theta(t),0\bigr),$$
   where $\lambda_{1}(t)=-\dfrac{m}{2l}\bigl(l\theta'(t)^{2}+g\cos\theta(t)\bigr)$ and $\lambda_{2}(t)=0$;
   the multipliers have dimensions $[\lambda_{1}]=\mu\tau^{-2}$ and
   $[\lambda_{2}]=\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$, so the reaction has force dimension,
   annihilates the virtual displacements, and has a unique multiplier;
3. in particular the reduced pendulum equation
   $\theta''=-(g/l)\sin\theta$ is exactly the Lagrange equation of
   $\widetilde L$, and every $C^{2}$ solution of it on such an interval $J$,
   with $x=X\circ\theta$, is an ideal constrained motion of the model.
items.strategy: Direct: verify the hypotheses of the reduction theorem, compute the substituted Lagrangian and its Lagrange equation, and evaluate the reaction and multiplier.
items.physical_scope: A worked check of the constraint-elimination theorem on the planar pendulum model: one particle of mass m constrained without friction to a circle of radius l in the plane z=0 under a uniform downward field; the periodic angle map from R is a surjective immersion onto the circle, and multiple angle representatives are allowed. It gives kinetic metric m l^2, substituted potential -m g l cos(theta), the pendulum equation theta-double-dot = -(g/l) sin(theta), and the reaction as the transpose constraint-Jacobian multiple with its two component multipliers. The constraint components have dimensions length squared and length, so their multipliers have different dimensions. All quantities are model values of the declared idealization.
